[[File:Ortega, Juan de – Tratado subtilissimo de aritmetica y de geometria, 1515 – BEIC 104004.jpg|thumb|right|Frontispiece of Ortega's ''Tratado'']]{{Short description|Spanish mathematician}}
'''Juan de Ortega''' (born [[Palencia]], Spain, c. 1480; died c. 1568),<ref name=catala>M A Catala, [https://www.encyclopedia.com/doc/1G2-2830903241.html "Ortega, Juan de"], Biography in ''Dictionary of Scientific Biography'' (New York 1970-1990).</ref> was a Spanish mathematician. He wrote some of the earliest works on commercial arithmetic, and discovered an improved method for calculating [[square root]]s.

==Life==
Very little is known of Ortega's life.<ref name="Smith1958">{{cite book|author=David E. Smith|title=History of Mathematics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=56lzDQAAQBAJ&pg=PA344|year=1958|publisher=Courier Corporation|isbn=978-0-486-20429-1|page=344}}</ref> He was a member of the [[Dominican Order]] in [[Kingdom of Aragon|Aragon]],<ref name="Smith1958" /> and he taught [[arithmetic]] and [[geometry]] in Spain and Italy.<ref name=catala />

==Mathematical contributions==
For his work on arithmetic Ortega drew on that of [[Boethius]] and of 13th-14th century mathematicians.<ref name=catala />

A widely known<ref name="Portugueses1994">{{cite book|author=Comissão Nacional para as Comemorações dos Descobrimentos Portugueses|title=Las relaciones entre Portugal y Castilla en la época de los descubrimientos y la expansión colonial|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t2Zyi4lXfN0C&pg=PA226|year=1994|publisher=Universidad de Salamanca|isbn=978-84-7481-792-8|page=226|language=pt}}</ref> publication among Ortega's works was ''Tratado subtilissimo de Aritmetica y de Geometria'' ("Most refined treatise on arithmetic and geometry") (Barcelona, 1512). The work was published in Spain, France and Italy, and translated into several languages.<ref name="Smith1958" /> The ''Tratado'' was innovative<ref name="Portugueses1994" /> in focusing on the practical, in particular commercial, application of arithmetical and geometrical techniques.<ref name="Smith1958" /> In later editions<ref>{{cite web|title=Biografia de Juan de Ortega|url=https://www.biografiasyvidas.com/biografia/o/ortega_juan.htm|publisher=Biografías y Vidas|accessdate=17 November 2017|language=es}}</ref> this work also introduces a novel [[Numerical analysis|approximation method]] for calculating [[square root]]s,<ref name="Smedley1845">{{cite book|author=Edward Smedley|title=Encyclopædia metropolitana; or, Universal dictionary of knowledge, ed. by E. Smedley, Hugh J. Rose and Henry J. Rose. &#91;With&#93; Plates|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EYXa49tpya4C&pg=PA436|year=1845|page=436}}</ref> which appears to be largely based on the [[Pell equation]] and thereby the best available technique,<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Benito|first1=Manuel|last2=Escribano|first2=Jose Javier|last3=Fernández|first3=Emilio|last4=Sánchez|first4=Mercedes|title=Fray Juan de Ortega's approximations, 500 years after|eprint=1212.1125 |date=5 December 2012|class=math.HO}}</ref> even though no general solution of this equation is known to have been found until much later.<ref name=catala />

Another textbook by Ortega was ''Cursus quattuor mathematicarum artium liberalium'' ("Course of four mathematical arts") (Paris, 1516).<ref name=catala />

Another textbook by Ortega was "Conpusicion de la arte de la arismetica y juntamente de geometría"<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Madrid |first1=María José |last2=Maz-Machado |first2=Alexander |last3=León-Mantero |first3=Carmen |last4=López-Esteban |first4=Carmen |title=Aplicaciones de las Matemáticas a la Vida Diaria en los Libros de Aritmética Españoles del Siglo XVI |journal=Bolema: Boletim de Educação Matemática |date=December 2017 |volume=31 |issue=59 |pages=1082–1100 |doi=10.1590/1980-4415v31n59a12 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
